topics.title: 3.1 Data Types & Variables
topics.description: Value vs reference types, common types, choosing a type, constants, var and naming rules.

questions.prompt: C# data types are divided into which two main groups?
Which are VALUE types? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: string, arrays and class instances are reference types.

questions.prompt: Which are REFERENCE types? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: A reference-type variable holds a reference to an object.

questions.prompt: What does this print?
questions.explanation: int is a value type: `b = a` COPIES the value. Changing b doesn't affect a.

questions.prompt: What does this print?
questions.explanation: Arrays are reference types: `second = first` makes both variables refer to the SAME array, so the change shows through `first`.

questions.prompt: string is a reference type, but a string cannot be modified in place.
questions.explanation: Strings are immutable: operations like `name + "!"` create a new string.

questions.prompt: Which declaration is correct for a float?
questions.explanation: Add f for float, m for decimal.

questions.prompt: Which declaration is correct for a decimal?
Which is correct for a char?
questions.explanation: Single quotes and exactly one character for char; double quotes for string.

questions.prompt: Which data type should store a TUITION FEE?
questions.explanation: decimal gives accurate decimal arithmetic for money.

questions.prompt: Which data type should store a student ID like "00142"?
questions.explanation: int would drop the leading zeros (00142 → 142).

questions.prompt: Which data type should store “Is payment complete?”
questions.explanation: Two logical states.

questions.prompt: Which data type should store a letter grade such as A?
questions.explanation: A single character.

questions.prompt: Which data type should store age in years?
questions.explanation: A whole number.

questions.prompt: Which line will NOT compile?
questions.explanation: PI is a constant, so it can't be reassigned.

questions.prompt: In `var year = 2026;`, what type does the compiler infer for year?
questions.explanation: var doesn't mean “any type” — the compiler infers it from the value. 2026 is an int.

questions.prompt: Which are INVALID as C# variable names? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Names can't start with a digit, and reserved keywords like class can't be used.

questions.prompt: In C#, `marks` and `Marks` are the same identifier.
questions.explanation: C# identifiers are case-sensitive.

questions.prompt: Which naming convention is used for LOCAL VARIABLES?
questions.explanation: camelCase for locals; PascalCase for types, methods and properties.

topics.title: 3.1 Type Conversion & TryParse
topics.description: Implicit vs explicit conversion, casting, Parse and the safe TryParse pattern.

questions.prompt: What kind of conversion is this?
questions.code:
int number = 25;
double result = number;
questions.explanation: int fits safely into double (25 → 25.0).

questions.prompt: What value does roundedDown hold?
questions.code:
double price = 19.95;
int roundedDown = (int)price;
questions.explanation: Casting a double to int removes (truncates) the decimal part: 19.95 → 19.

questions.prompt: Why does converting double → int need an explicit cast?

options.text: Because double is a reference type
Information (the decimal part) may be lost

questions.explanation: Explicit conversion: always consider loss of information.

questions.prompt: Which converts the text "42" into an int?
questions.explanation: Parsing turns text into a number. Casting a string to int doesn't compile.

questions.prompt: Which method safely converts text to int WITHOUT throwing an exception for invalid text?
questions.explanation: TryParse returns false instead of throwing a FormatException.

questions.prompt: The user types abc. What does this print?
questions.explanation: TryParse returns false, so the else branch runs.

questions.prompt: If the user types abc into `int.Parse(input)` instead, what happens?
questions.explanation: That's exactly why TryParse is safer.

questions.prompt: What does int.TryParse(input, out int age) do? (select all that apply)

options.text: Throws an exception for invalid input
Stores the converted number in age

questions.prompt: What does the `?` in `string? input` mean?

options.text: input may be null (e.g. if there is no input)

questions.explanation: Console.ReadLine() can return null, so the type is a nullable string.

topics.title: 3.1 Operators & Precedence
topics.description: Arithmetic, integer division, modulus, precedence, comparison and logical operators.

questions.prompt: What is `7 % 3`?
questions.explanation: % gives the remainder: 7 = 2 × 3 + 1.

questions.prompt: What is `7 / 3` when both are int?
questions.explanation: Integer division drops the remainder.

questions.prompt: What is `17 % 5`?
What does this print?
questions.explanation: Both are int, so 5 / 2 = 2 (integer division).

questions.prompt: What does this print?
questions.explanation: Casting a to double first makes it decimal division.

questions.prompt: What does this print?
questions.explanation: Tricky: `x / 2` is int / int = 3 FIRST, then stored in a double as 3 (printed as 3). Use `x / 2.0` to get 3.5.

questions.prompt: What is `2 + 3 * 4`?
questions.explanation: * happens before +: 3 × 4 = 12, + 2 = 14.
Parentheses first: 5 × 4 = 20.

questions.prompt: Which operator means NOT EQUAL to?
What is the difference between `=` and `==`?

options.text: = assigns a value; == compares two values

questions.prompt: With age = 20 and paid = false, what is `age >= 18 && paid`?
questions.explanation: && is true only if BOTH sides are true.

questions.prompt: With isMember = false and isStaff = true, what is `isMember || isStaff`?
questions.explanation: || is true if AT LEAST ONE side is true.

questions.prompt: With isRegistered = true, what is `!isRegistered`?
questions.explanation: ! reverses the value.

questions.prompt: In Student Profile v1, the user enters 150. What is printed?
questions.explanation: valid is true, but marks <= 100 is false, so the whole && expression is false.

questions.prompt: Campus Café: what does this print?
questions.explanation: 4.50 × 2 = 9.00, and :F2 formats to 2 decimal places.

questions.prompt: Why does the café app store unitPrice as decimal instead of double?

options.text: decimal gives accurate decimal arithmetic for money (no binary rounding errors)

topics.title: 3.2 Selection Statements
topics.description: Sequence, selection, iteration and jump; if-else, else-if grading, switch and the conditional operator.

questions.prompt: Match the four ways statements control execution — which are correct? (select all that apply)

options.text: Jump: changes the flow (break, continue, return)
Selection: chooses a branch based on a condition

questions.prompt: Processing 5 student marks one after another uses which kind of statement?
With marks = 49, what does this print?
questions.explanation: 49 >= 50 is false → else branch.

questions.prompt: With marks = 85, what grade does this assign?
With marks = 79, what grade does this assign?
With marks = 50, what grade does this assign?
questions.explanation: 50 >= 50 → C (the boundary counts).

questions.prompt: With marks = 49, what grade does this assign?
questions.explanation: None of the conditions are true → else → F.

questions.prompt: Why must the else-if conditions be checked from HIGHEST to lowest here?

options.text: C# requires numbers in descending order
Conditions are checked in order and the first true one wins — checking >= 50 first would give 85 a C

questions.prompt: What should you do BEFORE applying the grading rules?
questions.explanation: Otherwise 150 would get an A.

questions.prompt: The user types 4. What does this print?
questions.explanation: No case matches "4", so default runs.

questions.prompt: In a switch, what does `break` do?
When is a switch statement a good choice?

options.text: When one variable is compared against several exact values

questions.explanation: Ranges suit if/else-if better.

questions.prompt: What is status when m = 72?
questions.code: string status = m >= 50 ? "PASS" : "FAIL";
questions.explanation: `condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse` — 72 >= 50 is true.
